headline: Shift Large User Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates large energy users to pay for their grid infrastructure upgrades, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer groups, Governor Abigail Spanberger, environmental groups
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users
news_headline: Governor Signs Data Center Energy Cost Shift
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed legislation, including HB 1393, to protect Virginia ratepayers from shouldering the cost of new energy infrastructure investments by data centers. The bill requires costs for increased generating capacity to be passed on to customers with 25 MW or more in electric demand.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report monthly data center water consumption, increasing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, transparency advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New Law Requires Data Center Water Data
news_summary: A new Virginia law, identical to SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage. This data will be publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website starting January 1, 2027.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new data centers, including noise studies, and allows localities to assess broader environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups, local governments, Delegate Joshua Thomas
news_headline: Virginia Enacts Data Center Siting, Noise Rules
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval. This legislation provides a framework for localities to better manage data center development and its community impacts.
